Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

varm 0.1.0

First release. The package is experimental: the API may still change.

Bayesian VAR fixes

  • bvarm() sum-of-coefficients and single-unit-root dummy priors now use the p presample observations (as in BEAR, Sims and GLP) instead of observations p + 1 to 2p.
  • The single-unit-root dummy now covers exogenous and deterministic regressors, not only the constant.
  • The marginal likelihood with dummy priors now updates the dummy block’s posterior; hierarchical soc / sur hyperparameter inference changes accordingly.

0.1.0 API notes

The API was refactored to tidy principles and ggplot2. Outputs now follow broom column names; the object internals ($estimate, $bands, $B, $draws, …) are unchanged.

Breaking or renamed outputs

  • as.data.frame() on irf() / fevd() results (alias tidy(), as_tibble()): column h is now horizon; the wide q0.xx quantile columns are replaced by one row per cell and band level with conf.low and conf.high (bands = FALSE drops them). response and shock are factors in variable order.
  • lp_supt() data frame / tidy(): columns are response, horizon, estimate, std.error, band, level, conf.low, conf.high, with band equal to "sup-t" or "pointwise".
  • compare_lp_var(): column h is now horizon.
  • mcmc_diagnostics() tidy output: columns param, mean, sd are now term, estimate, std.error (plus ess, rhat, geweke_z).
  • irf_path(): columns median, lower, upper are now estimate, conf.low, conf.high (with date).
  • plot() methods return a ggplot (invisibly, after printing); base graphics are no longer used.

New

  • Generics re-exported from generics / ggplot2: tidy(), glance(), augment(), autoplot(). tidy() / as_tibble() methods for varm, IRF, FEVD, forecast, historical decomposition, bvarm, tvpvar, lpm and the lp_* results, mcmc_diagnostics; glance() for varm, bvarm, tvpvar, lpm, lp_state, lp_smooth, lp_panel, mcmc_diagnostics; augment() for varm.
  • autoplot() methods for IRF, FEVD, forecasts, historical decomposition, draws, MCMC diagnostics, bvarm, tvpvar (coefficients, volatilities, IRF at dates) and every local-projection result.
  • theme_varm(), varm_palette() (colour-blind safe) and normalise_to() (replaces the list form of normalise, which still works).
  • tidyselect arguments for variable names (lp(shock = , contemp = ), id_chol(order = ), autoplot(shocks = , responses = ), …), and a vars = argument of varm() for data frames.

Fixes

  • bvarm() works with soc / sur set to NULL in prior_minnesota().
  • id_restrictions(): the orientation of the solution is deterministic.
  • proxy_draws(): revised block-length rule of the moving-block bootstrap.
  • draws(bias_correct = TRUE) warns when combined with method = "mc" draws (it only applies to bootstrap draws).
  • irf.tvpvar() rejects id and warns when a requested date is out of sample.
  • tvpvar() warns when the prior degrees of freedom for Q do not exceed the number of coefficients + 1 (the prior mean of Q is then undefined, as with the default prior at p = 4).

Reduced-form VAR

  • varm(): OLS / Gaussian ML estimation of a VAR(p) with constant, linear trend and exogenous regressors; var_select() (AIC, HQ, SC, FPE); stability() (companion eigenvalue moduli); lag_matrices(); methods print, summary, coef, resid, fitted, vcov, logLik, nobs. Agrees with vars to about 1e-12 (coefficients, covariance, log-likelihood, information criteria, roots, Cholesky IRF, FEVD, point forecasts).
  • irf(), fevd(), hd() and forecast() as S3 generics with methods for varm, bvarm, varm_draws (irf, fevd) and tvpvar (irf, fevd, forecast); unit-impact normalisation, cumulative responses, percentile bands at several levels, autoplot(), plot() and tidy() for IRF and FEVD objects.
  • draws(): the common container (varm_draws) of reduced-form draws (B,Σ)(B, \Sigma) from the residual bootstrap, wild bootstrap (Rademacher or Mammen weights), Kilian bootstrap-after-bootstrap bias correction and the asymptotic normal / inverse-Wishart Monte Carlo.

Structural identification

  • id_chol(), id_longrun() (Blanchard-Quah), id_sign() (Haar rotations, Uhlig / Rubio-Ramirez-Waggoner-Zha), id_given().
  • id_zerosign(): sign plus zero restrictions (ARRW 2018 null-space sampler; the importance weights are not implemented, see the help page).
  • id_restrictions(): short-run and long-run zero (A-B style) restrictions.
  • id_hetero(): identification through heteroskedasticity, two regimes.
  • irf_fry_pagan(): Fry-Pagan median-target rotation.
  • Proxy-SVAR: id_proxy(), proxy_draws() (wild and moving-block bootstrap), proxy_fstat(), varm_proxy(), varm_proxy_robust() (weak-instrument robust confidence sets), varm_proxy_bayes() (limited-information Bayesian proxy-SVAR on bvarm() draws), varm_proxy_arw() (alias id_proxy_bayes, Arias-Rubio-Ramirez-Waggoner type posterior with exogeneity, relevance and sign restrictions) and varm_proxy_gkr() (Giacomini-Kitagawa-Read prior-robust bounds).

Bayesian VAR

  • bvarm() with prior_minnesota(): conjugate Normal-inverse-Wishart BVAR with Minnesota, sum-of-coefficients and single-unit-root priors; exact draws for fixed hyperparameters, optimiser plus adaptive random-walk Metropolis for the hyperparameters (Giannone-Lenza-Primiceri). The log posterior agrees with BVAR::bvar at matched prior scale to about 1e-13.
  • bvarm(prior = prior_triangular()): triangular equation-by-equation Gibbs sampler with Minnesota, SSVS or horseshoe priors, optional stochastic volatility (Kim-Shephard-Chib mixture, forward-filtering backward-sampling); volatility().
  • tvpvar() with tvp_prior(), irf_path(), tvp_volatility() and coef, summary, plot, irf, fevd, forecast methods: TVP-VAR with stochastic volatility and time-varying contemporaneous matrix (Primiceri training-sample calibration).
  • mcmc_diagnostics(): effective sample size, split R-hat, Geweke z-score for bvarm hyperparameters or user chains.

Local projections

  • lp(): local projections with Newey-West or HC1 standard errors, LP-IV (2SLS), lag augmentation, external shock series, cumulative responses. Matches lm + sandwich to about 1e-13.
  • lp_joint() (joint cross-horizon covariance), lp_supt() (sup-t simultaneous bands), lp_state() (state-dependent LP; matches lpirfs::lp_nl to about 1e-12), lp_smooth() (smooth LP), lp_panel() (panel LP with fixed effects and clustered errors), lp_forecast() (direct forecasts) and compare_lp_var().

Data

  • yraw: quarterly US inflation, unemployment and interest rate, 1953Q1-2006Q3 (Koop and Korobilis).

Engine

  • All estimators, bootstraps, samplers and identification loops are compiled (Rcpp / RcppArmadillo, files in src/).

Documentation and validation

  • Vignettes: getting-started, var-theory, identification, bayesian-var, tvp-var, local-projections, lp-advanced, choosing-a-method and validation (reproducible validation report with live comparisons against vars, BVAR, lpirfs, lm + sandwich and quoted simulation studies).
  • README rewritten with a feature matrix, benchmarks, validation table, limitations and a literature map; _pkgdown.yml lists every help topic once in grouped reference sections; docs-src/methods-index.md indexes every method with its definition and reference.
  • Test suite of 65 tests / 728 expectations (tests/testthat) and heavier scripts in validation/ (bayes.R, ident-extra.R, lp-extra.R, proxy-coverage.R, tvp.R; run the unit tests with Rscript validation/run-all.R).

Known limitations

See the “Limitations” section of the README and the validation report: under-coverage of draw-based IRF bands in short persistent or heteroskedastic samples, the proxy-SVAR wild bootstrap at impact, sup-t bands, slightly low stochastic-volatility calibration, slow mixing of the hierarchical-hyperparameter sampler, unweighted zero+sign draws, and no missing-value handling.
